claims.text: The WAL must be synced before content moves from the WAL into the database.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database

claims.text: The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.
claims.quote: and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL

claims.text: Rollback-journal COMMIT occurs when the rollback journal is deleted.
claims.quote: The COMMIT occurs when the rollback journal is deleted. The WAL approach inverts this.

claims.text: After a crash or ROLLBACK, the rollback journal restores the database to its original state.
claims.quote: In the event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the rollback journal is played back into the database file to revert the database file to its original state.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints available frames without waiting and syncs the database if all log frames were checkpointed.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL waits until there is no writer and readers use the most recent database snapshot.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.

claims.text: After its wait, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL checkpoints all log frames and syncs the database file.
claims.quote: It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the database file.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART waits until all readers read from the database file only.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE truncates the log file to zero bytes before successful return.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and provides access to frame-count output values.
claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.

claims.text: Each reader can have its own end mark while the WAL grows.
claims.quote: Because the WAL can be growing and adding new commit records while various readers connect to the database, each reader can potentially have its own end mark.

claims.text: A checkpoint stops when it reaches a WAL page past the end mark of any current reader.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.

claims.text: The checkpointer records its progress and resumes from that point on the next invocation.
claims.quote: The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.

claims.text: If overlapping readers always leave at least one reader active, checkpoints cannot complete and the WAL can grow without bound.
claims.quote: However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.text: Reader gaps are periods with no database readers when checkpoints can be attempted.
claims.quote: This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.

claims.text: By default, SQLite auto-checkpoints on a COMMIT at 1000 WAL pages or when the last connection closes.
claims.quote: By default, SQLite will automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes.

claims.text: Passing zero or a negative N to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.
claims.quote: Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.

claims.text: A checkpoint normally recycles the WAL by overwriting it from the beginning instead of truncating it.
claims.quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.

claims.text: When the last database connection closes, it checkpoints and deletes the WAL and shared-memory files.
claims.quote: When the last connection to a database closes, that connection does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file, to clean up the disk.

claims.text: The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.

claims.text: A large change to a large database can produce a large WAL file.
claims.quote: So a large change to a large database might result in a large WAL file.

claims.text: Read performance deteriorates as the WAL grows because readers check the WAL for content.
claims.quote: read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content

claims.text: Frequent checkpoints keep the WAL small and can maximize read performance.
claims.quote: To maximize the read performance, one wants to keep the WAL as small as possible and hence run checkpoints frequently, perhaps as often as every COMMIT.

claims.text: Infrequent checkpoints amortize checkpoint costs over more writes and can maximize write performance.
claims.quote: To maximize write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints infrequently and let the WAL grow as large as possible before each checkpoint.

claims.text: A WAL hook callback can invoke a checkpoint based on application-chosen criteria.
claims.quote: This callback can then invoke sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() or sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() based on whatever criteria it thinks is appropriate.

claims.text: Registering sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint().
claims.quote: Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.

claims.text: WAL readers and writers can run at the same time because writers append to the WAL.
claims.quote: Writers merely append new content to the end of the WAL file. Because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of readers, writers and readers can run at the same time.

claims.text: Only one writer can run at a time because there is only one WAL file.
claims.quote: However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.

claims.text: If another process holds the checkpoint lock, the call returns SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock on the database file. If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned.

claims.text: The busy handler is not invoked when the checkpoint lock cannot be obtained.
claims.quote: Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.

claims.text: A null or empty zDb requests the checkpoint operation on all attached WAL databases.
claims.quote: If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.

claims.text: On SQLITE_BUSY for one attached database, processing continues for the remaining attached databases and returns SQLITE_BUSY at the end.
claims.quote: If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.

claims.text: The write-ahead log implementation does not work on a network filesystem.
claims.quote: This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not work on a network filesystem.
